note:
Header banner candidates for /pages/our-philosophy. Malcolm, 2026-08-27: someone working in a lab, looking at the camera and smiling, background blurred by foreground focus.

THE BOX WAS MEASURED LIVE, NOT ASSUMED. The hero is full-bleed at a FIXED PIXEL HEIGHT: 440px at 1920/1512/1440, 400px at 1280/1024/768, 375px at 390. So the visible shape runs 4.36:1 on a wide monitor down to 1.04:1 on a phone, object-fit: cover, object-position 50% 50% (this page is NOT right-pinned - the collection pages are). Publishing master is therefore 3750x848 = 4.42:1, per the standing recipe.

GENERATED AT 2.909:1 AND CROPPED, NOT EXTENDED. 4096x1408 is the widest frame every supplier can approach: it sits under gpt-image's hard 3:1 refusal, both edges divide by 16, and Seedream still delivers it at full 4K. The 4.42:1 master is then cut as the CENTRAL 926-row band (y241-y1167) and scaled to 3750x848 - no canvas extension, which is the step with four separate failure modes on this project. That is why every brief below carries deliberate headroom above the head and room below the hands: the top 17% and bottom 17% of what is generated are thrown away.

SUBJECT SITS RIGHT OF CENTRE, HEAD AT ~0.7 ACROSS. The overlaid type on this page is CENTRED (both desktop and mobile) and runs about 740px wide - roughly the middle 38% of the frame at 1920. A head at 0.7 across clears it. It also survives the centred cover-crop: at 1440 the visible master window is x487-x3262 of 3750, at 1024 it is x789-x2961, and 0.7 x 3750 = 2625 sits inside both. No supplier is asked to compose around the type - the frame is stated as an edge condition instead, because 'leave the upper third quiet' is what put a black bar across a model's forehead on the FAQ page.

TWO LIGHTING REGISTERS, DELIBERATELY. P1/P4 are the bright airy clinical room the current banner already uses; P2/P3 are the low-key graphite room that matches the brand's dark hero register and gives white type somewhere to sit without a heavy overlay. The live overlay is 45, which is why the present banner reads as a grey rectangle - expect to drop it to ~22-25 and buy contrast with a local scrim instead.

NEGATIVES WERE WRITTEN FRESH, NOT INHERITED. The selfie waves' negative list bans 'no bokeh portrait mode, no shallow depth of field' - the exact opposite of this brief. Copying it forward would have quietly cancelled the one thing Malcolm asked for.

No references anywhere: no product, no packaging and no branding is in frame, so there is nothing for a reference to lock. Class B throughout.

BRIEF REVISED AFTER A SIX-SUPPLIER SMOKE TEST on P1, 2026-08-27 (originals kept in assets/ai-generated/2026-08-22-multi-page-philosophy-lab-scientist/smoke-r1/). All six returned a usable frame, which is the proof the brief was close - but three faults were common enough to be the brief's fault rather than the engines': flux2 rendered the whole bench in focus and readable, and luma and nbp_pro both put her dead centre. The position instruction sat six paragraphs down, which loses to a portrait prior - it now leads. Headroom was ignored by every single engine when stated as 'a quarter of the way down from the top edge', so it is now a RATIO to her own head height, which is the form that has held elsewhere on this project.

THE CENTRAL-BAND CROP PLAN DID NOT SURVIVE CONTACT. Every engine put the head 5-14% down rather than the 25% asked for, so cutting the 4.42:1 master from the exact middle of the generated frame decapitates the subject. The crop is AIMED per candidate instead - taken high, so it keeps the head with a little air and cuts at the chest. Still no canvas extension.

slots.title: Bright clinical room, woman, late thirties
slots.prompt:
A photograph of one woman at work in a cosmetic-chemistry laboratory, taken on a full-frame camera with a fast 85mm lens wide open. The picture is a wide horizontal band, close to three times as wide as it is tall.

SHE IS NOT IN THE MIDDLE OF THE PICTURE. She stands well over to the RIGHT, with her head about seven tenths of the way across from the left edge. The left half of the frame holds no person at all - it is the empty depth of the room going away from the camera. There is also a clear band of open room ABOVE her head, about as deep as her head is tall, so the top of her head is nowhere near the top edge of the picture.

WHO SHE IS: a woman of about thirty-eight, north-western European, with dark blonde hair pulled back into a low practical ponytail and a few strands loose at the temples. Light hazel eyes, straight brows, fair skin. She wears no makeup at all.

HER SKIN IS REAL AND UNRETOUCHED. Pores are visible across the nose and cheeks, there are fine lines at the outer corners of her eyes and one faint line across the forehead, a scatter of small freckles over the nose and cheekbones, two or three small moles, and faint natural unevenness of colour at the sides of the nose and along the jaw. The forehead and the bridge of the nose carry the ordinary sheen of real skin. Nothing about her face is smoothed, evened or softened.

SHE IS LOOKING STRAIGHT DOWN THE LENS AND SMILING. It is a genuine, warm, unforced smile that reaches her eyes and creases the skin at their outer corners, upper teeth just showing, lips relaxed. Not a wide grin, not a laugh, not a held pose - the expression of someone who has glanced up at a colleague she likes.

WHERE SHE IS IN THE FRAME: she stands to the RIGHT of centre. The centre of her head sits about seven tenths of the way across the picture measured from the left edge, and her body occupies roughly the right third. The whole left two thirds of the picture is the room itself, receding away from the camera.

HOW MUCH OF HER IS IN VIEW: there is generous open room above her - the clear gap between the top of her head and the top edge of the picture is about as deep as her head is tall, and nothing of her is cut off by the top edge - Head, shoulders, chest, both arms and both hands are all in view.

WHAT SHE IS DOING: she has paused mid-task and turned to the camera. She stands square to a long worktop that runs away from her into the left of the frame. One hand rests flat and easy on the worktop beside a small rack of plain clear glass vials; the other holds a slim glass pipette, tipped down and held loosely at waist height. Both hands are ordinary, correctly formed, five fingers each, and neither is doing anything strenuous.

WHAT SHE IS WEARING: a plain white laboratory coat, clean, well-fitted, sleeves at the wrist, worn open over a plain pale grey crew-neck top. There is nothing printed, embroidered, pinned or clipped on the coat anywhere, no badge and no card. The weave of the cotton is crisp and readable at the shoulder.

ONLY SHE IS SHARP - THIS IS THE POINT OF THE PICTURE. The plane of focus falls on her eyes. Her eyes, lashes, brows, lips, the loose strands at her temple and the fabric of her coat are crisp. Everything behind her dissolves: the length of worktop a metre back is already soft, and the far side of the room is completely unreadable - shapes, tone and light only, with not one legible edge, not one identifiable object and nothing written anywhere. What is nearest the camera at the very bottom of the frame is soft as well. Points of light on glass far behind her open into smooth round discs.

THE ROOM, WHICH REACHES EVERY EDGE OF THE PICTURE: a modern, bright, spotlessly clean laboratory. Bone-white walls, a long pale grey worktop, glass-fronted upper cabinets, ranks of tall clear glassware, and a wide window out of shot to the left throwing broad cool daylight straight across the room. Out of focus it reads as soft blocks of bone white, pale cool grey and very pale blue with small bright highlights where the light catches glass. The worktop runs off the bottom edge of the picture, the tops of the cabinets and the pale ceiling fill the top edge, and the room continues past the left edge and past the right edge as well. No part of the frame is a plain flat field of a single colour and nothing is empty.

LIGHT AND COLOUR: cool, even, clinical daylight, arriving mainly from her front left, modelling her face gently with soft shadow under the cheekbone and jaw and a soft catchlight in each eye. The whole picture is cool - bone white, pale grey, cool blue, the faintest hint of teal. No warmth, no golden cast, no orange.

It looks like a real photograph of a real working scientist, taken by a good photographer on an ordinary working day.

slots.title: Low-key graphite room, woman, early fifties
slots.prompt:
A photograph of one woman at work in a cosmetic-chemistry laboratory, taken on a full-frame camera with a fast 85mm lens wide open. The picture is a wide horizontal band, close to three times as wide as it is tall.

SHE IS NOT IN THE MIDDLE OF THE PICTURE. She stands well over to the RIGHT, with her head about seven tenths of the way across from the left edge. WHO SHE IS: a woman of about fifty-two, European, with dark brown hair going silver at the temples, cut to the jaw and tucked behind one ear. Brown eyes, olive-fair skin. She wears no makeup at all. She reads as senior and completely at ease - someone who has run a laboratory for twenty years.

HER SKIN IS REAL AND UNRETOUCHED, AND IT IS THE SKIN OF A WOMAN OF FIFTY-TWO. Clear lines fan from the outer corners of both eyes and deepen as she smiles, there are two soft horizontal lines across the forehead and a light line from each nostril to the corner of the mouth, the skin at the jaw is a little softer than it was, pores are visible on the nose and cheeks, and there are a few small moles and faint patches of uneven tone. This is a face that has aged normally and pleasantly. Nothing is smoothed, filled or airbrushed, and she is not made to look younger than she is.

SHE IS LOOKING STRAIGHT DOWN THE LENS AND SMILING. A genuine, warm, unforced smile that reaches her eyes and creases them, upper teeth just showing, lips relaxed. Not a wide grin, not a laugh, not a held pose.

WHERE SHE IS IN THE FRAME: she stands to the RIGHT of centre. The centre of her head sits about seven tenths of the way across the picture measured from the left edge, and her body occupies roughly the right third. The whole left two thirds of the picture is the room itself, receding away from the camera.

HOW MUCH OF HER IS IN VIEW: there is generous open room above her - the clear gap between the top of her head and the top edge of the picture is about as deep as her head is tall, and nothing of her is cut off by the top edge - Head, shoulders, chest, both arms and both hands are in view.

WHAT SHE IS DOING: she has paused mid-task and turned to the camera. She stands at a long dark worktop that runs away from her into the left of the frame. Both hands rest lightly on the worktop, one beside a small rack of plain clear glass vials. Her hands are ordinary, correctly formed, five fingers each, and they show her age as honestly as her face does.

WHAT SHE IS WEARING: a plain white laboratory coat, clean and well-fitted, worn open over a plain dark charcoal crew-neck top. Nothing is printed, embroidered, pinned or clipped on the coat anywhere, no badge and no card. Against the dark room the white coat is the second brightest thing in the picture after her face.

ONLY SHE IS SHARP - THIS IS THE POINT OF THE PICTURE. The plane of focus falls on her eyes. Her eyes, lashes, brows, lips, the silver at her temple and the weave of her coat are crisp. Everything behind her dissolves: the worktop a metre back is already soft, and the far side of the room is completely unreadable - shapes, tone and light only, with not one legible edge, not one identifiable object and nothing written anywhere. Points of light far behind her open into smooth round discs.

THE ROOM, WHICH REACHES EVERY EDGE OF THE PICTURE: a modern cosmetic-chemistry laboratory kept deliberately low-lit. Charcoal-graphite cabinetry, a dark slate worktop, dark walls, and deep shadow through most of the depth of the room. Far back there are a few cool blue-white sources - a strip of light under a cabinet and the pale glow of a screen turned away from the camera - and because they are so far out of focus they read as soft rounded pools of light rather than as objects. The field behind her is deep graphite and dark teal with those few cool highlights. The worktop runs off the bottom edge of the picture, the dark upper cabinets fill the top edge, and the room continues past the left edge and past the right edge as well. It is dim but it is not murky: there is depth and separation in the shadow, not a flat black wall.

LIGHT AND COLOUR: a single cool key light from her front left puts clean daylight-coloured light on her face and the front of her coat, with a soft shadow under the cheekbone and jaw and a soft catchlight in each eye. She is by a clear margin the brightest thing in the picture. The palette is cool throughout - graphite, dark teal, cool blue-white. No warmth, no golden cast, no orange, no tungsten.

It looks like a real photograph of a real working scientist, taken by a good photographer on an ordinary working day.
